scenes.heading: Checkpointing
scenes.narration: Let's take a deep look at Checkpointing and how it works under the hood in Spark.

scenes.heading: What checkpointing provides
scenes.narration: Checkpointing is how Structured Streaming survives failures and restarts. It persists the stream's progress, including which source offsets have been processed and the current state of any aggregations, to reliable storage. On restart, Spark reads the checkpoint to resume exactly where it left off, which is the basis of its exactly-once guarantees.

scenes.heading: Inside the checkpoint directory
scenes.narration: A checkpoint directory holds several subfolders that together capture the query's exact position. The offsets folder records the input range planned for each batch, while the commits folder marks which batches finished successfully. The state folder stores the running state for stateful operators like windowed counts. Together with the metadata, these let Spark reconstruct the query deterministically after a crash.

scenes.code:
q = (df.writeStream
       .outputMode("append")
       .option("checkpointLocation", "s3://bucket/chk/job1")
       .format("delta").option("path", "/delta/out")
       .trigger(processingTime="30 seconds")
       .start())
# Kill and restart: it resumes from committed offsets
scenes.heading: Setting a durable checkpoint
scenes.narration: The checkpointLocation must point to durable, shared storage such as S3 or HDFS, never local disk, so it survives node loss. With it set, you can stop and restart this query and it will resume from the last committed offsets without reprocessing or dropping data. Each streaming query needs its own dedicated checkpoint directory. Reusing one across different queries corrupts recovery.

scenes.heading: Streaming vs RDD checkpointing
scenes.narration: Streaming checkpointing captures offsets, state, and commit logs so a query can recover exactly-once. RDD checkpointing is a different, older mechanism that truncates a very long lineage chain by materializing an RDD to reliable storage, preventing costly recomputation in iterative algorithms. They share a name but solve distinct problems, and the streaming variant is mandatory for any writeStream sink.

scenes.text: Always point checkpointLocation at durable, unique storage.
scenes.narration: Losing or sharing a checkpoint directory breaks recovery guarantees, so treat it as critical infrastructure per query.
